Once upon a time, while we were travelling to the town, we saw that polythene was being used extensively in the town as well as in the countryside. That is when we collectively decided to do something about it.

That is when we thought of a plan. We were thinking of staying here for two days and that is when we saw a woman throwing vegetable and fruit peels in a polythene bag. We asked our mother to go speak to that woman and she agreed by saying “we’ll speak to everyone”.

After that we went to that woman’s house and told her that the usage of polythene can cost us our lives because when we burn polythene, it produces poisonous gases that can cause diseases like T.B, breathing trouble and much more.

The lady then asked “what else happens with the usage of polythene?” That is when we told her that if we use polythene on a fertile land, it can turn barren just like how a wheat crop won’t grow properly if we cover it up with polythene.
The lady understood the point that we made and thought of using a cloth bag instead of a polythene bag to store the wheat produce. This way, people slowly started reducing their usage of polythene.

I learnt all of this from my village, and today no one from my village is suffering from T.B or breathing problems because my village is free from polythene now. We all just have one slogan for other neighbouring villages - “Stop using polythene. Start living life.”
